scope.head: bee8868b9cc6a98149f7f428a38d29969ad45924
scope.range: Current uncommitted Stage B Host qualification and exact Pi native integration, compared with bee8868

findings.title: Native result consumption does not require a matching tool start event
findings.trigger: A stream contains a permission decision and a matching tool_execution_end event but no tool_execution_start event.
findings.impact: The parser can accept a completed native tool effect without evidence that the corresponding execution boundary was started, weakening protocol completeness and the pre-effect evidence chain.
findings.evidence: The completeness check only iterates over starts and verifies that each start has a later matching completion; it never verifies that every completion has a preceding matching start. The focused tests cover a completion without a decision, but not a completion without a start.
findings.suggestion: Require one-to-one matching start/end pairs by tool call ID and name, with each completion occurring after its start, and add a regression test for an end-only stream.

positive_observations: Focused tests cover malformed streams, terminal-state requirements, complete native tool inventory, matching permission decisions, denial outcomes, identity binding, and immutable configuration rechecks.
The retained native receipt records actual allowed write/read calls and five denied native attempts with matching permission decisions and completions.
The public no-bootstrap observation records the legitimate allowed result and absence of outside, shell, and authority markers.
limitations: The final release log ends after the Node test suite; npm audit completion and a final full-release status were not observed.
The receipt correctly records Bash curl as an execute event; no dedicated native Pi fetch callback is claimed or reviewed.
